summary: Interpreted the corrected receipt (CheckRun fc17700defb243bfad08ed6717fb32fd) and strengthened the account on both the comparison and caller sides. The comparison whose predicate is 'if the resolution is Ok then the decided entry at the returned index is the caller's entry' is now evaluated `violated` with valid witness index 9 and a complete witness, so a new Interpretation bound to that experiment asserts the scoped defect on an evaluated comparison plus both receipts of the lineage (joint_history explains they differ only in the emitted admission identity fields; the three cited events agree field for field). I also added the in-repo caller consequence as durable knowledge and two sources: the async example documents `append_notify` as confirming durability synchronously for a specific entry 'decided at its assigned index' and announces the returned index without re-reading the log there, while the existing runtime test only asserts a non-zero index and a non-empty suffix — so the shipped usage pattern relies on exactly the signal the lost-entry interleaving can deliver falsely, and no existing test pins the entry at the returned index. One further corrected execution is submitted with mode-specific result event names, because the control and mode-B comparisons came back `unknown` only due to my shared event name; their own events were already evaluated. Incomplete: that successor receipt is pending, and follower-origin assignments, batch_size > 1 and flexible quorums remain unmeasured.
